title: No CLI command to query execution history
description: Agents can execute proxied requests and receive execution_id in responses, but the platform provides no CLI command to retrieve or query execution records later. This breaks auditability and observability for agents.
reproduction_steps: Register and authenticate as an agent
Request access to a toolkit and get approved
Make a proxied request via `jentic execute` and note the execution_id returned
Attempt to query that execution record using `jentic execution get <id>` or similar commands
Observe that no such command exists
expected_behavior: Agents should be able to query their own execution history by execution_id or list recent executions.
actual_behavior: No CLI command exists to retrieve execution records. Execution IDs are returned but not queryable.
evidence: No execution history exposed via the CLI
Execution IDs are returned in responses but are not queryable later by the agent
This is a usability gap — users should be able to audit their own execution history

title: No CLI command or agent-accessible endpoint for audit logs
description: The platform tracks audit events internally but does not expose them to agents via CLI or API. Agents cannot view their own activity history or audit trail.
reproduction_steps: Register and authenticate as an agent
Perform several actions (register, request access, make proxied requests)
Attempt to view audit logs using `jentic audit` or `jentic logs` commands
Observe that no such command exists
Attempt to access audit events via direct API call
Observe that no agent-accessible endpoint exists
expected_behavior: Agents should be able to view audit events related to their own activity, including access requests, executions, and credential usage.
actual_behavior: Platform tracks audit events internally but provides no CLI command or API endpoint for agents to access them.
evidence: No audit command in the main CLI
Platform tracks activity internally but does not expose audit events to agents
Goal 11 is also blocked. There's no CLI command to view audit logs
